memos.headline: Broad Washout Across Universe; UNH and PG Stand Out as Relative-Strength Leaders
memos.body: I am looking at a universe where nearly every name is deeply oversold, with RSIs in the 20s and drawdowns of 20-37% from 52-week highs. The indiscriminate selling makes it dangerous to bottom-fish in the weakest relative-strength names—NVDA at RSI 28.5 and -37% from highs, AAPL at RSI 25.2 and -27% from highs, and CAT at RSI 22.0 and -31% from highs all show no sign of stabilization yet. The two clear standouts are UNH (RSI 58.4, +18.7% relative strength vs SPY over 4 weeks, only -16% from highs, and actually positive on the week) and PG (RSI 40.9, +15.7% 12-week relative strength, only -8.9% from highs), both trading near their 50-day and 200-day means rather than far below them. I have moderate conviction in these two defensive leaders and would avoid the broken momentum names until they reclaim their 50-day averages. MSFT is the most interesting of the beaten-down tech names given its +3.8% 4-week relative strength vs SPY, but I need to see it hold 350 before getting constructive.

Defensive leadership with +15.7% 12-week relative strength vs SPY, shallow -8.9% drawdown, and RSI 41 suggesting room to run—would exit below 155.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Show Superior Earnings Power; UNH and XOM Flash Margin Warnings
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+77.9% YoY revenue, 56.2% net margin) and GOOGL (+11.8% revenue, 27.5% margin with only $14.8B debt), both of which are converting top-line growth into outsized bottom-line gains. MSFT continues to compound at +12.3% revenue growth with a 34.6% net margin and manageable $45B debt, making it a reliable compounder. On the other side, UNH's 5.5% net margin and anemic +1.6% net income growth on $76.9B of debt concern me—any uptick in medical costs could compress cash flow further. XOM posted -1.1% revenue decline and a thin 9.1% margin, leaving little room for error if commodity prices soften. CAT's -5.0% revenue decline is a cyclical red flag, though margin discipline (17.2% net margin, +4.4% NI growth) partially offsets the concern.

11.8% revenue growth, 27.5% net margin, and a clean $14.8B debt load make this the best risk-adjusted earnings profile among mega-cap peers.
12.3% revenue growth and 34.6% net margin on $45B debt is a durable compounder; I'd reassess if cloud segment growth decelerates below high single digits.
88.3% YoY net income growth and margin expansion to 10.7% signal operating leverage is finally kicking in, though $58B debt warrants monitoring.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 4.50% as 10y Yields Plunge 59bp in 3 Months — Positioning for a Slowdown Regime
memos.body: I read the current macro regime as a late-cycle pause tilting toward easing. The Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three months while the effective rate has drifted down 15bp over the same period, and the 10y yield has dropped 59bp to 4.01%, signaling the bond market is pricing in growth deceleration or eventual cuts. CPI is running at 2.8% y/y — still above target but not accelerating — while unemployment has crept up 30bp over the past year to 4.2%, consistent with a softening labor market. The 10y-2y spread at +35bp has normalized sharply (+67bp y/y), which historically accompanies the transition from inversion to recession risk. A hot March jobs report or a re-acceleration in CPI above 3% would challenge this slowdown call, but absent that, I favor duration-sensitive quality growth and defensive staples over cyclicals and energy.

views.note: High-quality duration asset benefits from falling long rates and resilient recurring revenue in a slowdown.
Falling 10y yields support valuations for mega-cap growth, though consumer softening from rising unemployment is a modest headwind.
Defensive staples outperform in slowdown regimes; stable demand and lower discount rates are tailwinds.

Ad revenue is cyclically sensitive; lower rates are supportive but a slowdown in business spending could weigh on search budgets.

memos.headline: NVDA Post-Earnings Sentiment Shock Likely Priced; XOM Disclosure Cluster Warrants Monitoring
memos.body: I see limited GDELT-style media sentiment data in the evidence provided, so I am relying on 8-K filings and the one concrete price reaction as proxies for narrative shifts. NVDA's Q4 results 8-K on 2025-02-26 triggered an -8.5% two-day drawdown, suggesting the negative sentiment impulse was sharp but is now five weeks old and likely absorbed by the market. XOM filed three 8-Ks in the first three days of April—covering other events, officer changes, and Reg FD disclosure—an unusual clustering that could signal a narrative shift worth watching, though the tone is ambiguous. AAPL's February shareholder-vote filing and GOOGL's March Reg FD disclosure are routine and unlikely to move sentiment materially. I have low conviction across the board given the thin sentiment evidence, but NVDA's tone may be turning up from a deeply negative post-earnings base, while XOM's disclosure burst introduces uncertainty.

views.note: Post-earnings -8.5% sentiment shock is five weeks stale and likely priced; tone should be mean-reverting from a negative base.
Unusual cluster of three 8-Ks in three days introduces narrative uncertainty; watching for tone clarification before taking a directional view.
Routine shareholder-vote 8-K carries no sentiment signal; no reason to deviate from neutral.
Reg FD disclosure is standard corporate communication with no discernible tone shift.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Surges to Extreme Levels, Signaling Structural Tariff/Sanctions Risk Across Supply-Chain-Exposed Names
memos.body: I am writing with high concern: the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has spiked 162% over three months to 438.93, while VIX has nearly doubled to 30.02 and HY spreads have widened by 120bp over the same period—this is a regime-level shift, not a one-quarter event. The combination of extreme policy uncertainty with falling WTI crude (down ~10% over 3m to $67.43/bbl) suggests markets are pricing in demand destruction from escalating trade barriers rather than a supply shock, which is distinctly negative for globally exposed tech and industrials. I have highest conviction that names with deep China manufacturing or revenue exposure—AAPL, NVDA, CAT—face structural headwinds from tariff and export-control escalation; a reversal in my view would require a concrete de-escalation framework (e.g., tariff rollback or bilateral semiconductor agreement). XOM's two 8-K filings in the first week of April may relate to energy policy or sanctions-related disclosures, and the weak crude backdrop limits upside even if geopolitical supply risk re-emerges. For financials like JPM, widening credit spreads and steepening yield curve create a mixed picture, but policy uncertainty of this magnitude historically compresses multiples.

views.note: Extreme policy uncertainty and likely tariff escalation on China-assembled hardware create structural margin and supply-chain risk.
Export-control tightening on advanced semiconductors to China remains the dominant geopolitical risk; policy uncertainty at 439 reinforces this.
Global capex cycle vulnerable to trade-war demand destruction signaled by collapsing crude and surging uncertainty.
WTI at $67.43 and falling limits upside, but recent 8-K disclosures and potential geopolitical supply disruption keep me from outright avoiding.
Steepening curve (+15bp 1m) helps NII but HY OAS widening to 4.01% and extreme policy uncertainty cap conviction.
Less direct tariff exposure than hardware names, but antitrust and regulatory FD disclosure on Mar-18 warrant monitoring.
Domestic-demand defensive with pricing power; relatively insulated from tariff and export-control escalation compared to tech/industrials.
